changes.note:
Actual Phase 3 efficacy: 50; ORCA-2 randomized 810 adults. 12-week cytisinicline achieved continuous abstinence weeks 9-12 32.6% versus 7.0% placebo, OR 6.3 (95% CI 3.7-11.6); sustained weeks 9-24 21.1% versus 4.8%. Five placebo vs one treated patients needed antihypertensive rescue; prespecified SBP primary comparison was nonsignificant.; Source: https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/corcept-therapeutics-announces-third-quarter-financial-results-3; Benchmark: https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/45/38/3912/7741010; Uncertainty: Nominal secondary P values may not be familywise significant after a failed primary; no independently verified patient QoL or hard health outcome is established.

Nominal placebo-adjusted fasting glucose P=0.002 and body-weight P=0.0001 were favorable but are secondary.; Source: https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/corcept-therapeutics-announces-third-quarter-financial-results-3; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/multiple-endpoints-clinical-trials; Uncertainty: Missing full primary confidence interval, dropout-adjusted sensitivity and multiplicity hierarchy mean secondary robustness is not settled; known primary miss is an adverse inferential fact rather than an unknown.

GRACE NCT03697109 documented maintenance of hypertension control during 12-week blinded withdrawal in patients previously responding.; Source: https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/corcept-therapeutics-announces-third-quarter-financial-results-3; Benchmark: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13220893; Uncertainty: GRADIENT 22-week primary is negative, and no subsequent independent adrenal-only confirmation or longer blinded durability has been disclosed, but other relacorilant hypercortisolism subgroup signals exist.

changes.note:
Actual Phase 3 efficacy: 75; Exact MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 double-blind double-dummy 24-week active-control trial randomized 88 aficamten vs 87 metoprolol. Adjusted between-arm peak VO2 change +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1; P<0.001) at primary time point. 2026 prespecified follow-up exercise analysis found >=3.0 mL/kg/min improvements in 20.5% active versus 3.7% metoprolol; metoprolol arm average change was negative.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40888697/; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42624353/; Uncertainty: 175 randomized, 165 (94%) with core-lab validated CPET in later exercise analysis. Some mean contrast arose from deterioration under metoprolol, so superiority to beta blocker does not show equivalence to a placebo comparator or survival impact. Post-hoc/secondary contrasts do not replace the primary prespecified endpoint.
Clinical importance and patient benefit: 75; MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 aficamten vs metoprolol at 24 weeks: KCCQ-OSS adjusted mean difference +7.8 points (95% CI +3.3 to +12.3, P=0.001). A >=20-point health status gain occurred in 38.6% vs 18.4% (absolute difference +20.2 points; NNT ~4.9), and deterioration of at least five points occurred in 6.8% vs 18.4%.; Source: https://www.jacc.org/doi/full/10.1016/j.jacc.2025.10.059; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33183512/; Uncertainty: CI for mean OSS effect includes <5 points and self-reported health status is subjective; adverse outcome differences, missing questionnaire reporting and generalizability to all HCM cases remain relevant.
Statistical reliability: 50; MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 primary between-arm pVO2 +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1; P<0.001); NYHA, KCCQ, LVOT gradient, NT-proBNP and LAVI secondary outcomes favored aficamten, while left ventricular mass index difference was nonsignificant.; Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2504654; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/multiple-endpoints-clinical-trials; Uncertainty: A significant primary contrast and consistent secondary outcomes support efficacy, but confidence intervals and multiplicity for every secondary and sensitivity to missing data have not been independently audited as a separate research question.
Replication and durability: 50; MAPLE NCT05767346 randomized 88 aficamten versus 87 metoprolol with 24-week adjusted peak VO2 difference +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1, P<0.001). The separate SEQUOIA trial reported a 24-week placebo-adjusted +1.7 mL/kg/min, 95% CI +1.0 to +2.4.; Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2504654; Benchmark: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2401424; Uncertainty: Positive short-term direction replicated with different controls, but 52-week MAPLE treatment durability, all subgroup interaction CIs, and comparative long-term cardiac safety require more evidence.
Safety and tolerability: 50; MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346: any serious AE 7/88 (8%) aficamten vs 6/87 (6.9%) metoprolol; withdrawal due to AE 1.1% vs 3.4%. LVEF<50% by core laboratory 1/88 versus 0/87, while mean LVEF change was -5.3% active vs -0.5% metoprolol. One sudden death after brief viral illness occurred in aficamten group and requires context, not automatic drug attribution.; Source: https://ir.cytokinetics.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/Cytokinetics-Presents-Additional-Data-from-MAPLE-HCM-at-the-Hypertrophic-Cardiomyopathy-Medical-Society-Scientific-Sessions-and-American-Heart-Association-Scientific-Sessions-2025/default.aspx; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39056349/; Uncertainty: Small active-control sample limits risk precision; near-equal serious AE incidence does not prove long-term safety equivalence. Ejection fraction reduction and monitoring burden are substantive risks.
Equal 20% weights. Research only, not FDA probability. Exact-NCT snapshots retained in repository.

Difference -34 percentage points, OR 0.17 (95% CI 0.04-0.77), P=0.022. The prespecified primary hypertension endpoint was met, but the prespecified design target was a 50 percentage-point contrast; secondary hyperglycemia analyses were not statistically significant.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41730814/; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22466348/; Uncertainty: Randomized-withdrawal population was response enriched following 22 weeks of open-label treatment: 62 randomized overall, 43 evaluable for hypertension endpoint. Missing endpoint values classified as lost response (roughly 23% missing across arms); modified ITT and per-protocol sensitivity analyses still favored relacorilant. Wide OR confidence limits, selection/generalizability, protocol revisions, and unknown longer-term durability prevent strong efficacy calibration.
Clinical importance and patient benefit: 50; GRACE NCT03697109 randomized-withdrawal hypertension responders: loss of BP control 11/21 (52%) on continued relacorilant vs 19/22 (86%) after placebo substitution, 34 percentage points favoring treatment. Ambulatory SBP adjusted between-arm difference -6.5 mmHg (95% CI -11.9 to -1.1; P=0.019) in evaluable paired subset.; Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13220893/; Benchmark: https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/45/38/3912/7741010; Uncertainty: The cohort was selected for response during prior open-label treatment, so results do not establish population-wide patient benefit. Patient-reported physical function, hospitalization and survival improvement not demonstrated in these randomized data.
Statistical reliability: 50; GRACE NCT03697109 hypertension loss primary ITT OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.77, P=0.022 (11/21 vs 19/22). Modified ITT 9/19 vs 15/18 (P=0.029), per-protocol 7/15 vs 15/18 (P=0.032). Trial treated missing week-12 data as loss of response; only 62 total subjects randomized after open-label enrichment.; Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13220893/; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/multiple-endpoints-clinical-trials; Uncertainty: Primary analysis and two sensitivity subsets remain conventionally significant, but small n, original co-primary endpoint amendment, and selected study population limit certainty.
Replication and durability: 50; In GRACE, 11/21 continued relacorilant vs 19/22 placebo-substituted patients lost BP control by week 12, showing a sustained on-treatment contrast in selected patients. Independent GRADIENT NCT04308590 had relacorilant SBP reduction -6.6 versus -2.1 mmHg placebo but the between-group primary comparison was nonsignificant.; Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13220893/; Benchmark: https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/corcept-therapeutics-announces-third-quarter-financial-results-3; Uncertainty: The open-label treatment period and short randomized-withdrawal window do not establish long-term randomized maintenance in all hypercortisolism etiologies. Different etiology and trial design limit direct cross-study reproducibility.
Safety and tolerability: 50; GRACE randomized-withdrawal safety: back pain 5/30 versus 6/32, headache 3/30 versus 4/32, acne 3/30 versus 0, bursitis 3/30 versus 0, and withdrawal discontinuation 5/30 versus 5/32. No hypokalemia, adrenal insufficiency, endometrial hypertrophy bleeding, or drug-induced QT prolongation observed in the trial.; Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13220893/; Benchmark: https://ir.corcept.com/news-releases/news-release-details/corcept-therapeutics-announces-third-quarter-financial-results-3; Uncertainty: Earlier GRACE open-label stage had 57/152 discontinuations for multiple reasons including AEs and withdrawal. A small selected 12-week randomized population does not establish rare or long-term safety or peer drug superiority.

Actual Phase 3 efficacy: 75; Exact MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 double-blind double-dummy 24-week active-control trial randomized 88 aficamten vs 87 metoprolol. Adjusted between-arm peak VO2 change +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1; P<0.001) at primary time point. 2026 prespecified follow-up exercise analysis found >=3.0 mL/kg/min improvements in 20.5% active versus 3.7% metoprolol; metoprolol arm average change was negative.; Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40888697/; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42624353/; Uncertainty: 175 randomized, 165 (94%) with core-lab validated CPET in later exercise analysis. Some mean contrast arose from deterioration under metoprolol, so superiority to beta blocker does not show equivalence to a placebo comparator or survival impact. Post-hoc/secondary contrasts do not replace the primary prespecified endpoint.
Clinical importance and patient benefit: 75; MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 aficamten vs metoprolol at 24 weeks: KCCQ-OSS adjusted mean difference +7.8 points (95% CI +3.3 to +12.3, P=0.001). A >=20-point health status gain occurred in 38.6% vs 18.4% (absolute difference +20.2 points; NNT ~4.9), and deterioration of at least five points occurred in 6.8% vs 18.4%.; Source: https://www.jacc.org/doi/full/10.1016/j.jacc.2025.10.059; Benchmark: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33183512/; Uncertainty: CI for mean OSS effect includes <5 points and self-reported health status is subjective; adverse outcome differences, missing questionnaire reporting and generalizability to all HCM cases remain relevant.
Statistical reliability: 50; MAPLE-HCM NCT05767346 primary between-arm pVO2 +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1; P<0.001); NYHA, KCCQ, LVOT gradient, NT-proBNP and LAVI secondary outcomes favored aficamten, while left ventricular mass index difference was nonsignificant.; Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa2504654; Benchmark: https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/multiple-endpoints-clinical-trials; Uncertainty: A significant primary contrast and consistent secondary outcomes support efficacy, but confidence intervals and multiplicity for every secondary and sensitivity to missing data have not been independently audited as a separate research question.
